questions.stem: A 45-year-old male patient was given Hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone for Addison’s disease. Which of the following adverse effects are not seen with the use of mineralocorticoids?
questions.solutionHtml:
Hyper kalemic alkalosis
  • Fludrocortisone causes hypokalemic alkalosis not hyperkalemic.
  • Hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone are given for Addison’s disease.
  • Fludrocortisone is a potent mineralocorticoid having some glucocorticoid activity as well.
  • It acts on the kidney to secrete H+ and K+ in urine in exchange for Na+ ions. causing retention of Na+ and water and hypokalemic alkalosis.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 314,317.

questions.stem: Fludrocortisone is used for idiopathic postural hypotension and also to prevent salt wasting in congenital adrenal hyperplasia. The drug has the following activity:
questions.solutionHtml:
Both of the above

Fludrocortisone is a potent mineralocorticoid having some glucocorticoid activity as well.

Indication for using Fludrocortisone-

  • Replacement therapy in Addison’s disease.
  • Congenital adrenal hyperplasia in patients with salt wasting.
  • Idiopathic postural hypotension


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 314

questions.stem: Usually, glucocorticoid drugs with zero Mineralocorticoid activity are used in cerebral edema, as they don’t retain Na and water. So among the following, which glucocorticoid drug has zero Mineralocorticoid activity?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dexamethasone
  • Glucocorticoid drugs with zero mineralocorticoid activity are used in cerebral edema, as they don’t retain Sodium and water.
  • E.g.Dexamethasone/betamethasone is used in cerebral edema due to tumors, TB meningitis.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 314

questions.stem: A 45-year-old woman complained to her physician of weight gain, mild but continuing facial acne, and pigmented striae on her abdomen. Further exams led to the diagnosis of Cushing syndrome, and pharmacotherapy was prescribed. Which of the following drugs would be most appropriate to treat the patient’s disease?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ketoconazole
  • In patients with Cushing syndrome, the main goal of pharmacotherapy is to block glucocorticoid secretion.
  • Ketoconazole is an antifungal In doses higher than those employed in antifungal therapy, the drug inhibits cytochrome P-450 enzymes, thus blocking several steps of steroidogenesis.
  • As a result, the drug is the most effective inhibitor of steroid biosynthesis.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 319.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man suffering from non-Hodgkin lymphoma was hospitalized for his first cycle of chemotherapy. Pharmacotherapy was prescribed to prevent chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. The drug regimen most likely included ondansetron, aprepitant, and which of the following drugs?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dexamethasone
  • The best and most common regimen to prevent chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting is a three-drug combination of a serotonin 5-HT3 receptor antagonist, a glucocorticoid such as dexamethasone, and aprepitant; which is a NK-1 blocker.
  • This combination prevents acute emesis in 80 to 90% of patients and delayed emesis in more than 70% of patients.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 314,317.

questions.stem: A 35-year-old woman, 29 weeks pregnant, was admitted to the obstetrical unit with ruptured membranes. The patient was treated with nifedipine to delay premature labor and with another drug to accelerate the maturation of the fetal lungs, thus decreasing the incidence of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome. Which of the following drugs was most likely administered?
questions.solutionHtml:
Dexamethasone
  • Dexamethasone is used commonly in preterm delivery to decrease the incidence of neonatal respiratory distress syndrome.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 316.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old woman complained to her physician of a recent progressive loss of vision. The patient had been suffering from myasthenia gravis for 7 months and was being treated with prednisone, azathioprine, and neostigmine. Other medications taken by the patient included omeprazole for gastroesophageal reflux disease and lovastatin for hyperlipidemia. Further exams of the eye led to the diagnosis of glaucoma. Which of the drugs taken by the patient would be relatively contraindicated at this time?
questions.solutionHtml:
Prednisone
Prednisone is a corticosteroid
  • Corticosteroids are well known to cause cataracts and exacerbate glaucoma during long-term administration.
  • They are therefore contraindicated or should be used very cautiously, in patients with glaucoma.
  • Topical steroids are more commonly associated with glaucoma;
  • while systemic steroids are more commonly associated with cataracts.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:317,318.

questions.stem: For a patient who is receiving a long course of glucocorticoid and who now wishes to discontinue the drug, gradual tapering of the glucocorticoid is needed to prevent:
questions.solutionHtml:
The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis suppression
  • Occurs depending both on the dose and duration of therapy.
  • In time, the adrenal cortex atrophies.
  • Stoppage of exogenous steroid precipitated withdrawal syndrome consisting of malaise, fever, anorexia, nausea, postural hypotension, electrolyte imbalance, weakness, pain in muscles and joints, and reactivation of the disease for which the steroid was used.
  • Subjected to stress, these patients may go into acute adrenal insufficiency leading to cardiovascular collapse.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 318,319.

questions.stem: A patient was given an inhalation steroid for the management of chronic asthma along with bronchodilators. Which of the following adverse effects is of particular concern in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Oropharyngeal candidiasis
  • Hoarseness of voice, dysphonia, sore throat, and asymptomatic or symptomatic oropharyngeal candidiasis are the most common side effects of using Inhalational Corticosteroids. These can be minimized by the use of a spacer, and by gargling after every dose (to wash off the drug deposited on oral and pharyngeal mucosa).
  • Oral candidiasis can be prevented as well as treated by topical nystatin/clotrimazole.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:250.

questions.stem: A 45-year-old female came to OPD complaining of heartburn and pain in her stomach. She has a history of taking steroids for some allergic infections. By what mechanism does corticosteroid exert anti-inflammatory action which is also responsible for the reported adverse effect?
questions.solutionHtml:
Phospholipase A2
  • Glucocorticoids induce the production of lipocortin which inhibits phospholipase A2 which leads to a reduction in the synthesis of prostaglandins, and leukotrienes which are important mediators of inflammation.
  • Due to a decrease in the production of PGE2 and PGI2 which provide protection to gastric mucosa get hamper ultimately chances of peptic ulcer increase.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 310.

questions.stem: A patient was suffering from some infectious condition for which he was given some antimicrobial therapy along with corticosteroids. In which condition this can be indicated except:

options.label: B
options.text: Severe P. carinii pneumonia in AIDS patient

questions.solutionHtml:
Herpes simplex keratitis
  • Herpes simplex keratitis is an Absolute contraindication of corticosteroids use.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number:314-319.

questions.stem: An 18-year-old male high school baseball player is Interested in improving his hitting ability. He receives twice-weekly injections of anabolic steroids. Over the Next year, which of the following effects would be Likely observed in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Premature epiphyseal long bone closing
  • Use of anabolic steroids, (e.g., DHEA) by athletes can Cause premature closing of the epiphysis of the long Bones, which stunts growth and interrupts development.
  • High doses taken by young athletes may result in a reduction of testicular size, hepatic abnormalities (adenoma; not hemangioma), increased aggression, major mood disorders, and other adverse effects described earlier.


Essentials Of Medical Pharmacology, By KD Tripathi, 8th Edition, Page Number: 317-319.
